summary: A target-level plan for all seven stages: finite cyclotomic units and their regulator index; classical class-field and control comparisons; the conditional Vandiver module isomorphism; Baker–Brumer, abelian Leopoldt and an independent all-prime Ferrero–Washington route; and the Burns–Flach/Kurihara complex and integral determinant theorem. Generic completed algebra, cochains, determinants and inverse-limit exactness retain their existing owners. Three explicitly delimited source/proof gaps and precise supplier contracts remain; no implementation is claimed.

nodes.title: The norm relation for the inertia-generated kernel
nodes.statement: For m beyond eventual total ramification, H_m=ker(Y∞→A_m) has finite index in Y∞. If n≥m, H_n=ν_(n,m)H_m with ν_(n,m)=ω_n/ω_m=Σ_(i=0)^(p^(n−m)−1)γ^(ip^m). Consequently #A_n=#A_m·#(H_m/ν_(n,m)H_m). Y∞ and H_m are finitely generated torsion Λ-modules with the same μ and λ.

Raising inertia lifts to p^(n−m) powers gives the norm sum ν_(n,m); this proves equality of the closed generated kernels in both directions.
The inertia-control sequence makes Y∞/(p,T) finite; compact Nakayama gives finite generation. A positive free Λ-rank would make the displayed transition quotients infinite, so Y∞ is torsion.

nodes.title: The Baker–Brumer auxiliary polynomial
nodes.statement: Under a minimal hypothetical algebraic-coefficient relation among n≥2 Q-independent logarithms of algebraic p-adic units α_i, power the α_i deeply enough and solve log α_n=Σ_(i<n)β_i log α_i with algebraic p-integral β_i. For arbitrarily large h choose a nonzero integer coefficient polynomial P in n variables, degree at most L=⌊h^(2−1/(2n))⌋ in each variable and coefficients bounded by exp(2h³). Set F(z)=Σ_λ c_λ∏_(i<n)exp((λ_i+β_iλ_n)z_i log α_i). Its normalized algebraic jet rows vanish on the initial diagonal grid (qℓ,…,qℓ), 1≤ℓ≤h, total jet order ≤h², for a fixed q=p^a>exp(8D), D the coefficient-field degree.

Count the algebraic linear equations in c_λ: a fixed field-degree multiple of h times the number of jets of order ≤h², strictly less than (L+1)^n for h large.
Apply the imported relative Siegel estimate and its coefficient-height bound to get a nonzero integer solution. Use deep exp/log to identify normalized derivatives with algebraic polynomial rows.

nodes.title: Baker–Brumer extrapolation and nonvanishing
nodes.statement: For the auxiliary F above, let ε=1/(4n). For 0≤J≤12n, all normalized jets of total order ≤h²/2^J vanish at the diagonal points qℓ with 1≤ℓ≤h^(1+εJ), using integer floors. At J=12n this supplies at least (L+1)^n consecutive zeros of the diagonal exponential polynomial; the Vandermonde matrix forces two distinct monomial bases ∏α_i^(qλ_i) to coincide, contradicting Q-independence of their logarithms.
hypotheses: All constants are fixed before h. The algebraic evaluation lower bound includes denominator and archimedean-conjugate bounds.
proofSteps: For each derivative restrict to the diagonal and apply the p-adic normal-series Schwarz–Mahler estimate on the unit disc, with multiplicities at the previous grid in the ball |z|≤q^−1.

Compare its small upper bound with the product-formula lower bound for a nonzero normalized algebraic jet. Rousseau Lemma 2 supplies the dependence exp(2Dh³), the grid height and the derivative denominator. With q>exp(8D), the inequality is contradictory for h large at every induction step.
Halve the derivative budget while increasing the grid to h^(1+εJ), retaining the factorial bridge; prove the elementary inequalities uniformly for J≤12n.
At the last stage apply finite Vandermonde linear independence. A collision of bases gives Σ(λ_i−λ_i′)log α_i=0 with a nonzero integer tuple.

nodes.title: Equidistribution of p-adic digit truncations
nodes.statement: Let q=p for p odd and q=4 for p=2; let s_n(x) be the least nonnegative residue of x modulo qp^n. nodes.title: Greenberg’s cyclotomic conjecture
nodes.statement: For a totally real number field E and prime p, Greenberg(E,p) is the conjectural assertion μ(E∞/E)=λ(E∞/E)=0 for the cyclotomic Z_p-extension. Its formal equivalent is that the p-primary orders #Cl(E_n){p} are bounded. For abelian E, Ferrero–Washington reduces this assertion to λ=0 but does not prove it.
hypotheses: The general assertion is recorded as a conjecture; the equivalence is a theorem about the defined invariants.
proofSteps: Apply the general growth theorem with μ,λ nonnegative: bounded orders force both to vanish, and their vanishing makes the eventual order constant.
A finite initial segment does not affect boundedness. Separate the p-primary order from the full class number and the cyclotomic tower from a general Z_p-extension.
